facts.statement: Trinisaura fossils were found on James Ross Island, off the coast of northern Antarctica.
facts.quote: in what is now James Ross Island off the coast of northern Antarctica near Patagonia

facts.statement: The fossils of Trinisaura were collected in 2008 by paleontologists Juan Moly and Rodolfo Coria from the Snow Hill Island Formation.
facts.quote: The fossils were collected in 2008 by paleontologists Juan Moly and Rodolfo Coria from the sandstone of the Snow Hill Island Formation

facts.statement: Trinisaura remained undescribed in the Museo de La Plata collections until it was formally described by Coria and colleagues in 2013.
facts.quote: It remained undescribed in the collections of the Museo de La Plata until its description by Coria and colleagues in 2013

facts.statement: The genus name Trinisaura honors Argentine geologist Trinidad 'Trini' Diaz and the Latin root for 'lizard'.
facts.quote: The genus name is to commemorate the efforts of Argentine geologist Trinidad "Trini" Diaz and the Latin root -sauros, meaning "lizard"

facts.statement: The species name santamartaensis refers to Santa Marta Cove, the location where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: The species name is after Santa Marta Cove, where the fossils were collected

facts.statement: Trinisaura is classified as a basal member of the ornithopod clade.
facts.quote: Trinisaura has been classified as a basal (early-diverging or "primitive") member of the clade Ornithopoda

facts.statement: The only known skeleton of Trinisaura belongs to a subadult individual estimated to be 1.5 meters long.
facts.quote: Its only known skeleton comes from a subadult, with a small size of 1.5 m

facts.statement: Trinisaura was a lightly built, bipedal dinosaur with long legs adapted for running and a rigid tail for balance.
facts.quote: Trinisaura was very lightly built and bipedal, with long legs built for running and a rigid tail to aid in balance during locomotion

facts.statement: Trinisaura exhibited a slower growth rate than contemporaries in warmer climates, likely an adaptation to the cold Antarctic environment.
facts.quote: Trinisaura is also noted to have a slower growth rate than genera that lived in warmer climates, an adaptation to colder temperatures of the Antarctic

facts.statement: Trinisaura evolved distinct traits due to geographic isolation after Antarctica broke off from the supercontinent Gondwana.
facts.quote: During Trinisaura's existence, Antarctica had just recently broken off from the rest of Gondwana, causing it to evolve distinct traits due to geographic isolation

facts.statement: During the Upper Cretaceous, Antarctica had a much warmer climate than today and was covered in forests.
facts.quote: The climate during the Upper Cretaceous was much warmer than it is today, and the continent was blanketed in forests

facts.statement: Based on its phylogenetic position and skeletal remains, Trinisaura was a herbivore.
facts.quote: Based on the phylogenetic position of the genus within Elasmaria and the known material, Trinisaura was herbivorous

facts.statement: Trinisaura had an elongated neck ending in a small, beaked skull adapted for eating plants.
facts.quote: The neck was elongated, terminating in a small, beaked skull adapted for herbivory

facts.statement: The known fossils consist of a semi-articulated partial skeleton including vertebrae, an incomplete pelvis, a right humerus, and a partial right hindlimb.
facts.quote: The fossils come from a small ornithopod, consisting of a semi-articulated partial skeleton including several vertebrae (backbones), incomplete pelvis, fragmentary scapulacoracoid, right humerus, and a partial right hindlimb

facts.statement: Additional fossils, including the left scapulacoracoid and more vertebrae, were identified in 2019.
facts.quote: Later, however, more fossils including the left scapulacoracoid and additional vertebrae were noted to be known in 2019

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Trinisaura is deposited at the Museo de La Plata under catalogue number MLP-III-1-1.
facts.quote: The ornithopod specimen was then deposited at the Museo de La Plata under catalogue number MLP-III-1-1, later the holotype

facts.statement: It is debated whether the larger dinosaur Morrosaurus is a junior synonym of Trinisaura, despite several differentiating characteristics.
facts.quote: The much larger Morrosaurus, named in 2016, has been suggested to be a junior synonym of Trinisaura, though several characteristics differentiate the two genera

facts.statement: A 2022 analysis by Karen Poole found no Elasmaria clade, instead placing Trinisaura in a branch of Rhabdodontoidea with Patagonian and South African genera.
facts.quote: However, a 2022 phylogenetic analysis by Karen Poole of the ornithischian groups Iguanodontia and basal Neornithischia found no Elasmaria clade, instead with Trinisaura in a branch of Rhabdodontoidea containing the Patagonian genera Talenkauen and Anabisetia and the South African genus Kangnasaurus

facts.statement: Trinisaura was much smaller than the other named Antarctic ornithopod, Morrosaurus, which was approximately 4 meters long.
facts.quote: This is much smaller than the only other named Antarctic ornithopod, Morrosaurus, which was around 4 m long, differentiating the two in this aspect

facts.statement: Histological studies show that Trinisaura exhibited rapid growth with periodic interruptions, similar to other Antarctic ornithopods like Gasparinisaura.
facts.quote: The study confirmed this pattern in elasmarians, with comparison to the South American elasmarian Gasparinisaura finding incredibly similar histology to the Antarctic genera.

facts.statement: Trinisaura provides evidence linking ornithopod dinosaurs across the continents that formed the ancient supercontinent Gondwana.
facts.quote: The discovery of Trinisaura was concurrent with the first evidence of a previously hypothesized uniting clade of ornithopod dinosaurs from the continents that had comprised Gondwana.

facts.statement: Trinisaura and related fossils suggest that southern Gondwanan continents acted as a refuge for dinosaur species that were less successful elsewhere during the early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: These discoveries of connected endemic Gondwanan ecosystems have overturned the traditional view of the southern continents, acting as a refugium for animals more successful elsewhere earlier in the Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Trinisaura lived approximately 72 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous Campanian stage in what is now Antarctica.
facts.quote: Trinisaura santamartaensis es la única especie conocida del género extinto Trinisaura de dinosaurios ornitópodos que vivieron a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 72 millones de años, durante el Campaniense en lo que ahora es la Antártida.

facts.statement: The species Trinisaura santamartaensis was described and named in 2013 by Coria, Moly, Reguero, Santillana, and Marenssi.
facts.quote: La especie tipo Trinisaura santamartaensis fue descrita y nombrada en 2013 por Coria, Moly, Marcelo Reguero, Sergio Santillana y Sergio Marenssi.

facts.statement: The specific name refers to Caleta Santa Marta, a cave on the northeast coast of James Ross Island where the specimen was excavated from hard sandstone.
facts.quote: El nombre específico hace referencia a la Caleta Santa Marta, una cueva en la costa noreste de la isla James Ross donde el espécimen fue excavado en la superficie, enterrado en arenisca dura.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MLP-III-1-1 was found in the Snow Hill Island Formation, which dates to the Late Campanian, about 72 million years ago.
facts.quote: El holotipo , MLP-III-1-1, se encontró en la Formación Snow Hill Island que data del Campaniense tardío, de unos 72 millones de años.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton lacking a skull, including vertebrae, ribs, chevrons, parts of the shoulder girdle, forelimb bones, hindlimb bones, and foot phalanges.
facts.quote: Consiste en un esqueleto parcial sin cráneo. Se conservan vértebras, tres vértebras sacras del sacro, tres juegos de dos, tres y dos vértebras caudales, dos costillas, dos cheurones, la parte inferior de un omóplato derecho, un hueso de una clavícula derecho, el húmero derecho, dos metacarpianos, ambos ilion, el pubis derecho, el isquion derecho, el fémur derecho, la parte inferior de la tibia derecha, la parte inferior del tercer metatarsiano derecho, la primera falange del tercer dedo del pie derecho y la tercera y cuarta falange del cuarto derecho dedo del pie.

facts.statement: The holotype belongs to an immature individual and is part of the collection at the Museo de la Plata.
facts.quote: Pertenece a un individuo inmaduro y forma parte de la colección del Museo de la Plata.

facts.statement: The holotype is a subadult individual about 1.5 meters long, while an adult could have reached about 2 meters.
facts.quote: El holotipo, MLP-III-1-1, consiste en un esqueleto parcial que carece del cráneo, de un individuo subadulto de cerca de 1,5 metros de longitud, un ejemplar adulto podría haber alcanzado unos 2 metros.

facts.statement: Trinisaura was likely bipedal and relied on speed and agility to avoid predators.
facts.quote: Probablemente era bípedo y dependía de la velocidad y la agilidad para evitar a los depredadores.

facts.statement: A unique feature of Trinisaura is a scapula with a lower front edge projection called the acromial process, which ends in a sharp spike with a strong, sharp comb on the outside, relatively longer than in any other euornithopod.
facts.quote: Uno de ellos es una autapomorfia, una característica derivada única, la escápula tiene una proyección en el borde frontal inferior, el proceso acromial, que termina en una punta afilada en forma de espiga, esta tiene un peine fuerte y afilado en el exterior y es relativamente más largo que cualquier otro euornitópodo conocido.

facts.statement: The humerus has a vestigial deltoid crest reduced to a bump on the front exterior, and the humeral shaft bends strongly outward.
facts.quote: El húmero tiene una cresta deltopectoral que es vestigial y se reduce a una protuberancia en el frente exterior. El eje del húmero se dobla fuertemente hacia afuera.

facts.statement: The ischium bends gradually downward along the entire length of its axis.
facts.quote: El isquion se dobla gradualmente hacia abajo en toda la longitud del eje.

facts.statement: The preserved humerus is 112 millimeters long, thin, and hollow inside.
facts.quote: El húmero tiene una longitud conservada de 112 milímetros. Es delgado y hueco por dentro.

facts.statement: The scientific name of the species is Trinisaura santamartaensis.
facts.quote: name: Trinisaura santamartaensis

facts.statement: The genus Trinisaura was established by Coria et al. in 2013.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Coria et al., 2013

facts.statement: Trinisaura is classified within the infraorder Ornithopoda.
facts.quote: infraordo: Ornithopoda

facts.statement: Trinisaura is known only from the Gamma Member of the Snow Hill Island Formation on James Ross Island, located on the northeastern edge of the Antarctic Peninsula.
facts.quote: Trinisaura is known solely from the Gamma Member of the Snow Hill Island Formation in James Ross Island, an island in the James Ross Island group on the northeastern edge of the Antarctic Peninsula.

facts.statement: The fossils of Trinisaura show minimal transport and reworking, indicating they were deposited in a setting with little disturbance.
facts.quote: Trinisaura's fossils bear some surface weathering and abrasion, which indicate that they went through minimal transport, reworking, and subaerial weathering.

facts.statement: Wood fragments, twigs, and leaves found in concretions near Trinisaura fossils suggest they arrived via the same ocean currents that transported the dinosaur carcasses.
facts.quote: In the Gamma Member, wood fragments, twigs, and leaves have been found in concretions from the locale, associated with dinosaur fossils like Trinisaura itself and apparently came with the same ocean currents that brought the dinosaur carcasses.

facts.statement: The environment may have included wet areas similar to peat bogs, evidenced by fossils of peat mosses, clubmosses, firmosses, and Ericaceae.
facts.quote: Some of the environment may have been wet and similar to peat bogs, as evidenced by the presence of Sphagnaceae (peat mosses) and several other groups including the clubmoss Selaginella, the firmoss group Lycopodiaceae, and the clade Ericaceae.

facts.statement: The same formation has yielded fossils of the armored ankylosaur Antarctopelta, a sauropod vertebra, an aquatic elasmosaurid, and carnivorous mosasaurs Taniwhasaurus and Hainosaurus.
facts.quote: The Gamma Member of the formation has yielded several other fossil remains, such as the armored ankylosaur Antarctopelta, a vertebral centrum of a lithostrothian sauropod, an aquatic elasmosaurid, and the carnivorous tylosaurine mosasaurs Taniwhasaurus and Hainosaurus.

facts.statement: Asteraceae pollen grains collected from the formation represent the oldest known records of that plant family.
facts.quote: From the Gamma Member, Asteraceae pollen grains were collected that are the oldest records of the family.

facts.statement: The ilium of Trinisaura was elongated and low with a wavy upper edge.
facts.quote: El ilion es alargado y bajo con un borde superior ondulado.

facts.statement: The iliac blade was half the length of the ilium.
facts.quote: El ala es la mitad de la longitud.

facts.statement: The pubic bone had an appendix shaped like a tip projecting forward and downward.
facts.quote: El apéndice del hueso púbico tiene la forma de una punta que sobresale hacia adelante y hacia abajo.

facts.statement: The femur was robust, straight when viewed from the front, and angled forward when viewed from the side.
facts.quote: El fémur es robusto, recto en vista frontal, inclinado hacia adelante en vista lateral.

facts.statement: The lower part of the femur was strongly widened.
facts.quote: La parte inferior del fémur está fuertemente ensanchada.

facts.statement: The lower part of the third metatarsal bone had parallel sides and was flattened from front to back.
facts.quote: La parte inferior del tercer hueso metatarsiano tiene lados paralelos y está aplanada de adelante hacia atrás.

facts.statement: The first phalanx of the third toe had a robust shape with both the top and bottom widened.
facts.quote: La primera falange del tercer dedo tiene la forma robusta habitual con la parte superior e inferior ensanchadas.

facts.statement: The describers placed Trinisaura basally within the Euornithopoda group.
facts.quote: Los descriptores ubicaron a Trinisaura basalmente en los Euornitópodos.

facts.statement: A cladistic analysis indicated a position in the family tree above Gasparinisaura and below Talenkauen.
facts.quote: Un análisis cladístico indicó una posición en el árbol genealógico por encima de Gasparinisaura y por debajo de Talenkauen.

facts.statement: In 2015, it was discovered that Trinisaura formed part of the basal iguanodontid group Elasmaria.
facts.quote: En 2015, junto con varios otros ornitópodos patagónicos y antárticos, se descubrió que formaba parte del grupo basal de iguanodontidos, Elasmaria.

facts.statement: The parent group of Trinisaura is Elasmaria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Elasmaria

facts.statement: Trinisaura belongs to the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Trinisaura lived from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Although Trinisaura is the first euornithopod reported from the formation, similar basal forms were widespread in Upper Cretaceous Antarctica.
facts.quote: Aunque Trinisaura es el primer euornitópodo informado de la formación, los hallazgos de otras formaciones muestran que tales formas basales de euornitópodos estaban muy extendidas durante el Cretácico Superior de la Antártida.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Trinisaura is a basal iguanodontid, as this depends on the position of Thescelosaurus neglectus.
facts.quote: Trinisaura aparece como ornitópodo, pero se necesita saber la posición de Thescelosaurus neglectus para determinar si es un iguanodonte basal.
